abstract: MEX3A is essential for binding to Ago2/miR-126-5p and inhibition of apoptosis in endothelial cells implicated in cardiovascular health. Here, we discovered that the KH1 domain within the RNA binding region of MEX3A exists in equilibrium with an unfolded conformation. Using NMR spectroscopy and biophysical analysis, we dissect the KH1 folding kinetics and show that increased KH1 stability correlates with higher RNA affinity. The unfolded state of KH1 enables phosphorylation of T162, locking the domain in the unfolded conformation and enables recognition by 14-3-3 {zeta}. Residues in MEX3A KH1 that reduce its stability are located outside the RNA-binding interface and are evolutionary selected compared to human MEX3 paralogs. Semi-stability of KH domains in MEX3A and other multi-KH proteins may provide a general mechanism to tune RNA binding, enable phosphorylation and regulate biological function.
